summary: The accepted ownership and target-preservation plan survives this bounded restructuring attack, but its required AN.3/SV.2 dependency reversal is not applied by the current atlas build. One medium integration finding: the old edge survives and the intended new supplier edge is skipped, even though AN.3 is annotated as importing SV.2. The resulting graph is acyclic, not the accepted dependency graph. This is another concrete case of the mechanism reported in RT-RS-15/1; coordinate the implementation fix rather than creating competing fixes.

Both decompositions remain partial. The proposal/review preserve Tate Z1-Z3 admissibility, residue qualifications, the near-line Artin route, unresolved zero-free/explicit-formula proof gates, the quartic I/J/height interface, orbit-to-Selmer comparison, Davenport uniformity and infinite-local-condition tails. This check does not certify their source proofs or complete the future node migration.

Re-fetched Bhargava-Shankar arXiv:1006.1002v3 on 2026-09-24, SHA-256 7670970aca5df135af4ab4da926d3b2e3acc937dd5a6c918f802552c528712cf. Read Proposition 2.6 and the accompanying multiset reduction on printed p.12, and the minimal-pair/height comparison on p.22. GN.4's assigned Davenport contract retains projection-volume error and dependence on dimension, multiplicity and polynomial complexity; ST.0 retains 27 H(E) = 4 H'(E) on the specified minimal-pair carrier. No inference of uniform moving-region counting from mere homothetic asymptotics is made.

Inspected the outside-family supplier/consumer stage contracts AC.4, AL.0-3, CN.4, ES.4, GN.4, ML.3, PS.1, PM.0 and GlobalNumberFields Layer 9. Recomputed every direct surviving consumer of AN.0/AN.1/AN.6: exactly PM.0, SV.0, AN.2, AN.7 and PS.1, each with explicit replacement imports. Every suppliedBy entry for a narrowed layer has its corresponding proposal link. Unaffected prerequisites and the extra LD.3/AA.2 inputs to AN.8 are not deleted by the proposed ledger.

Independently checked the full native 3508-edge graph: applying the report's removal ledger and all 58 proposal links gives an acyclic 3545-edge graph (including UPSTREAM source-address vertices). The raw ledger removes 11 edges; one is LI.2 -> AN.0 from an already retired roadmap, explaining the prior review's 10 active removals. Simply adding the links without removing AN.3 -> SV.2 creates a cycle. Ran actual apply_restructurings with RS-07 alone and with all promoted proposals, and full build.assemble(require_distances=False); the old edge persists and the reverse edge is absent in all three. The 16 skipped UPSTREAM-address links are not confused with the one rejected real-stage edge.

Validation: check_restructure on the accepted input, check_redteam on this result, intake check-files on the two deliverables, 58 unit tests covering restructuring/red-team/queue/intake, and independent conservation/reachability/integration assertions. No Lean file is requested or changed; no Lean elaboration or proof-completion claim. Only the two RT-RS-07 deliverables are submitted.

findings.claim: The accepted large-sieve/zero-density ownership reversal is not effective in the build. AN.3 is narrowed with SV.2 in suppliedBy, but SV.2 still requires AN.3 and the actual SV.2 -> AN.3 supplier edge is absent. The engine applies the scope annotation while skipping the dependency that supplies its retained zero-density/mean-value route. This is a mismatch between the accepted plan and its integration, not a mathematical cycle in the intended restructuring.
findings.evidence: At 9bafe01650e531e445ddc4c723d239c061dfb6ee, RS-07.result.json's AN.3 rationale says 'Remove the old AN.3 -> SV.2 edge before adding SV.2 -> AN.3'; SV.2 similarly says to delete the old requires AN.3. RS-07.md section 6 makes that removal mandatory. scripts/restructure.py initializes its edge/reachability sets from the old snapshot (lines 36-39), writes narrow/drop metadata (lines 73-89), then rejects a new link when reaches(target, source) (lines 98-105), with no old-edge-removal step. Read-only execution with RS-07 alone and all promoted proposals leaves AN.3 -> SV.2 and records [SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2, AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3] in RS-07 skippedLinks. These runs add respectively 31 and 29 new stage edges; 16 other skipped entries are UPSTREAM addresses, not this failure. Full build.assemble reproduces old-edge true/new-edge false and the corresponding requires mismatch. Removing the old edge before inserting the intended links passes independent acyclicity checks. Reproduction and precise expected assertions are in RT-RS-07.md.
findings.fix: Have the maintainer/authorized integration fixer encode and apply the accepted edge-removal ledger atomically before adding replacement links, updating stageEdges, requires, consumers and the reachability index consistently. In this case remove AN.3 -> SV.2, retain SV.1 -> SV.2 and the existing AN.2 -> AN.3 input, then add SV.2 -> AN.3 while preserving the AN.3/SV.2 -> SV.3 downstream route. Test RS-07 alone, all promoted proposals and full assembly for old-edge absence, new-edge presence and matching scope/import metadata. Preserve all source nodes and provenance when separately processing the dropped construction stages; do not fabricate stage nodes for UPSTREAM library addresses or edit immutable Tau Ceti anchors. Coordinate this generic integration fix with RT-RS-15/1. Merely rerunning promotion/schema validation, appending the reverse edge to the old graph, or marking this valid supplier as intentionally skipped does not implement the accepted plan.
